newsitem.title: CHINA: Two quakes hit China, no casualties reported.
newsitem.headline: Two quakes hit China, no casualties reported.

text.p: Two earthquakes capable of causing heavy damage in a populated area rocked widely separated parts of China on Saturday, but officials said there were no immediate reports of casualties.

A quake measuring 5.0 on the Richter scale jolted China's eastern Fujian province, about 150 km (90 miles) northwest of the major port city of Xiamen at 2.51 p.m. (0651 GMT), an official said. The centre of the tremor was near Yong'an city and Fujian's border with Guangdong province, he added.
"Some people felt it but some didn't even know there was an earthquake," the official said.
"In general, the effect wasn't all that great," he said by telephone.
The official Xinhua news agency said the quake had damaged some buildings in Yong'an city and Liancheng county but the official said there were no reports of damage in Xiamen.
"We were well-prepared in Xiamen and evacuated everyone," he said. A media official in Yong'an, about 25 km (15 miles) from the epicentre, said there were no reports of injuries or damage as of yet.

Earlier, Xinhua said a tremor measuring 5.3 on the Richter scale had rocked a remote and sparsely populated area in the northwestern region of Xinjiang on Saturday, but it did not say if there were any casualties or damage. That area is around 2,500 km (1,500 miles) northwest of Yong'an city.

Chinese scientists say China has entered a period of high seismological activity and officials have forecast more quakes of more than six on the Richter scale for Xinjiang, which lies at the meeting of two seismological belts. A quake of that magnitude could cause widespread damage.
About 50 people have been killed in a series of tremors to rock the arid desert region that is home to many cotton farmers and sheepherders.

China suffered the worst quake in modern history on July 28, 1976, when a magnitude 7.8 hit the northeastern city of Tangshan, almost levelling it and killed at least 240,000 people. The most devastating earthquake in recorded history hit China's Shaanxi province in 1556, killing 830,000 people.
